correctness.rationale: For every available-vertex subset S and named player, the minimax recurrence in RESULT.md considers every edge of the induced graph, removes its endpoints, switches players and counts one move. The base case is zero for no legal edge. Induction on |S| proves the recurrence computes optimal terminal matching size. verify_bottomup.cpp visits every one of 2^n masks (up to 1,048,576 for the dodecahedron) and every legal transition. Independently verify_recursive.py uses formula-generated graphs and memoized search. Both code artifacts were executed, agree exactly on the complete JSON in checks.json, and verify all opening-edge and second-response histograms. The icosahedral and dodecahedral graph representations were checked as isomorphic to standard constructions.

originality.rationale: The principal earlier study (Cranston et al., arXiv:1208.0085) proves general bounds and explicitly realizes the octahedron as K6 minus a perfect matching; no novelty is attributed to that case. Its general results do not determine game values (5,6) for the icosahedral graph and (8,9) for the dodecahedral graph or the unique and eightfold second-player replies. Searches in the mathematical-result index and bibliographic literature found no exact or dominating calculation for the dual pair. The 2018 matcher game and the general saturation game are distinct edge-selection protocols. This is a best-knowledge priority comparison rather than a uniqueness guarantee.
residual_risks: An unindexed paper, computational appendix or equivalently labelled polyhedral game calculation may already contain these two scores or second-response counts.
Only one direct original preprint was inspected in full; the later matcher/saturation papers were inspected sufficiently to identify different game protocols, not exhaustively for all examples.
No independent scholarly verification or literature-priority certification has been conducted.

value.rationale: The five Platonic graphs form a natural complete collection, and their game scores separate first-move neutrality (tetrahedron/cube) from strict disadvantage (octahedron and both dodecahedral–icosahedral duals). The two duals demonstrate reversed starting advantage while occupying different positions relative to their ordinary maximum matching sizes. Exactly one successful Max second move out of 21 on the icosahedron, versus eight out of 25 on the dodecahedron, gives a sharp strategy-sensitivity contrast that cannot be inferred from the general one-unit theorem or ordinary matching numbers. The work is an exact fully reproduced classification of a motivated family, albeit finite.
